summary: SSID probe-response storm triggers wpa_supplicant restarts, causing VPN and DNS resolution failures for office clients
description:
Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10 08:15 PDT several office clients on the floor BYO Wi‑Fi (SSID: Redwood-Employee) experienced sudden VPN drops followed by DNS failures and inability to reach internal services. Symptoms correlated with frequent wpa_supplicant restarts on affected endpoints.

Impact: Multiple engineers lost active SSH/tmux sessions to internal systems and observed timeouts for dev tooling that relies on internal DNS. Roughly 20–30 clients intermittently affected over a ~2 hour window; baseline connectivity returned after controller-side mitigation.

Initial hypothesis: Clients receive an excessive burst of 802.11 probe responses from nearby APs (probe-response storm) triggering wpa_supplicant crash/restart cycles which tear down user-space VPN tunnels (WireGuard/Okta/SSO agents) and cause DNS resolver state to be lost.

Environment: Office Wi‑Fi (controller: Meraki MX + MR series), WPA2-Enterprise (802.1X/EAP-PEAP), client OS mix: macOS 13/14, Ubuntu 22.04, Windows 11. VPN clients observed: WireGuard (internal), Okta VPN agent, and system-level IPsec.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Be connected to Redwood-Employee SSID on office floor.
2) Trigger a background wireless scanning tool or drive a test AP that emits probe responses (test harness available in runbook).
3) Observe client wpa_supplicant/syslog for repeated restarts and VPN agent logs for session tear-down.
4) Confirm DNS resolver entries are flushed or timeouts occur immediately after wpa_supplicant restart.

Note: reproduction should be done in controlled test bay to avoid impacting production users.
logs_and_evidence:
- macOS Console excerpt (device: rjones-mbp):
  Mar 10 08:21:35 rjones-mbp wpa_supplicant[724]: wlan0: received probe response from 02:11:22:33:44:55 (multiple per second)
  Mar 10 08:21:36 rjones-mbp wpa_supplicant[724]: wpa_supplicant[724]: signal 11 (Segmentation fault)
  Mar 10 08:21:36 rjones-mbp kernel: WireGuard: wg0: interface down
  Mar 10 08:21:36 rjones-mbp okta-vpn[1987]: control connection lost, reconnecting

- Ubuntu 22.04 syslog (device: dev-ubuntu-07):
  Mar 10 08:19:12 kernel: wlan0: received 120 probe responses in 10s from AP 02:11:22:33:44:55
  Mar 10 08:19:12 NetworkManager[1123]: wpa_supplicant crashed, restarting
  Mar 10 08:19:12 wg-quick[1502]: wg0: interface brought down by system

- Controller metrics (Meraki): sudden spike in probe-response frames seen on floor AP group 3 between 08:15–08:30 PDT. Channel utilization briefly increased to 85%.

- Packet capture (AP-tap): burst of 802.11 management frames with identical SSID and varying source MACs; many malformed / unexpected IE sequences suggesting a misconfigured test AP or rogue device.
investigation_notes:
- Verified correlation between probe-response spikes (controller) and client wpa_supplicant restarts (endpoint logs).
- Reproduced in test bay with a rogue test AP emitting frequent probe responses with malformed IEs; clients began restarting supplicant after ~30s.
- Observed that wpa_supplicant on Linux/macOS crashed on parsing malformed 802.11 IE; stack trace points to parsing function when handling roaming candidate frames.
- VPN agents do not gracefully survive interface resets caused by supplicant crash: they teardown TUN/WG interfaces and require manual restart in some cases.
- DNS resolver (systemd-resolved / mDNSResponder) caches were flushed on interface restart causing transient name resolution failures until rebind.
- Hypothesis: a misconfigured in‑range device (lab AP or older vendor AP) is responding to probes too aggressively and with malformed information causing client supplicant parser to hit an unhandled error path.

Evidence collected: endpoint core dumps (collected from Ubuntu device), controller probe-response trace, AP-radio packet captures, and affected client list from NAC logs.
mitigation_taken:
- Network team temporarily blacklisted the rogue AP MAC on floor AP group and issued a controller firmware rollback to block malformed probe responses at the controller layer.
- On affected endpoints, support pushed an MDM script to restart VPN services and wpa_supplicant where necessary.
- Security team scanned floor for additional rogue radios; none found.
- Short-term policy applied: controller will drop probe-responses with malformed IE fields.
resolution:
Root cause: an older test AP in a nearby lab had been placed into a debug mode that broadcasted malformed probe responses at high frequency; client supplicant implementations lacked defensive parsing for the malformed IE leading to crashes.

Fix applied: test AP removed from office RF space and reconfigured; controller rule added to silently drop malformed probe responses; wpa_supplicant version pinned on Linux images to a patched build (see PR).

Rollout notes: corporate images updated with patched wpa_supplicant (deploy via MDM for macOS and scripted apt deployment for Ubuntu). Wireless controller rule deployed to all office clusters to filter malformed management frames.
postmortem_follow_up:
- Create automated detector in wireless controller to alert on probe-response rate anomalies and malformed IE frequency.
- Backport defensive parsing patch to the supported wpa_supplicant builds and publish CVE if required.
- Add test-cases in QA that simulate malformed management frames to ensure clients don't crash.
- Update runbook to include 'rogue probe-response storm' scenario and include safe reproduction lab steps.
- Verify VPN agents to better handle sudden interface down events (graceful reconnection).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:05 - Ethan Brooks: Assigned. Collected endpoint core dumps and controller pcaps. Reproduced crash in isolated bay; sending stack trace to security and wireless teams.

2026-03-10 10:12 - Priya Singh (Wireless): We saw a small cluster of APs in lab VLAN that had debugging mode enabled. Blacklisted MAC 02:11:22:33:44:55 and reduced probe-response flood. Controller now shows normalized utilization.
2026-03-10 11:40 - Carlos Mendes (Security): Confirmed rogue device was an old vendor AP used for RF testing. Device removed. Recommend we audit devices in labs adjacent to production floors.
2026-03-11 08:23 - SRE Team: Filed PR to add defensive filter at the controller layer to drop malformed management frames: https://github.com/redwood-inference/networking/pull/482
2026-03-12 15:00 - Ethan Brooks: Deployed patched wpa_supplicant to Ubuntu images and MDM script for macOS. Monitoring for recurrence; no new events in past 24 hours.
next_steps:
- Finalize and merge wpa_supplicant patch to stable branch and prepare advisory.
- Automate detection rule in controller and add Slack alert to #network-ops.
- Schedule audit of lab RF devices and update inventory tagging to prevent tests in production RF zones.
- Close ticket after 7 days of clean telemetry.
